evidence:
Frozen seed .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r11/task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (28549 bytes, sha256 a1c65c806b54da99a37ab2b5f455ede0a9385a09569903fb3a7f3446f7e83740) is byte-identical (cmp) to solution/app/src/seed_data.json; same hash is listed for solution/app/src/seed_data.json in qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r11/raw-evidence-index.json. It is the only shipped data file (template environment/assets/seed_data.json is a CHANGE_ME placeholder replaced by the task). Parsed in memory with Python json and checked by script:
(1) Referential integrity: 10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages, 3 notes, 6 reads; no duplicate ids or emails. Every job recruiter_id resolves to a recruiter and manager_id to a hiring_manager; every application job_id resolves and stage is in the 6 stages; every message application_id/sender_id, note application_id/author_id and read user_id/application_id resolves. No orphan rows.
(2) Rule consistency against environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md: positions per (job,stage) are contiguous 1..n; Interview counts 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 are within interview_limit; no duplicate email per job (Noor on JOB-PLAT and JOB-DSGN, allowed by rules s2 'same person may apply to different jobs'); only APP-301 is REJECTED and it carries rejected_from=SCREEN plus a non-blank reject_reason, no stray reject fields elsewhere; candidate_status_labels keys equal stages and match rules s7 table; thread_page_size 30 matches s6/s9. Every message sender is a legitimate participant (recruiter, that job's manager, or the application's own candidate); no blank bodies; timestamps sorted with no duplicates within each conversation; APP-101 has 120 messages (matches tests/app_context.md:29-30 '120 messages at the start'). Notes authors are allowed writers (MGR1 on JOB-PLAT, REC1, MGR3 on JOB-DSGN). Every read_count <= conversation length. Candidate accounts map by email to applications with matching names (CAN1->APP-101,APP-302; CAN2->APP-201; CAN3->APP-301).
(3) Agreement with graders: Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 of 3 with message 3 from REC3 gives 1 unread, matching tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:344 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread'; seeded JOB-PLAT order Applied Greta/Ade/Marco, Screen Priya/Samuel and Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' match functional prompt Z and judge.toml:416.
(4) Synthetic/clean: all emails use RFC 2606 reserved domains (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example); names are generic; no phone, address, DOB, ID number or URL. No password, token, API key or other credential appears in the seed (the demo password lives in the brief and solution/app/src/db.js:63 per the delivery profile and internal annotation 'If task data itself contain credential flag it'). Regex scan of every string for markup, script/javascript:, template syntax, SQL comment/DROP, prompt-injection phrases, secrets and URLs found only generated_note mentioning /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which is benign. All strings are printable ASCII.
Minor observations (not defects): (a) read markers USR-CAN1 on APP-101 (119 of 120) and USR-REC3 on APP-301 (2 of 3) precede a message the same person sent; the rule 'sending counts as having read' would place them at the end, but rules s6 also says own messages are never unread, so observable unread/seen values are identical either way and no grader depends on Noor's starting count; the golden unread query (solution/app/src/index.js:133, sender_id<>?) handles it. A naive count-minus-marker app would show Noor 1 unread, which is a genuine rule violation, not a seed defect. (b) APP-301 is REJECTED yet REC3's 2026-07-29 message says 'We will write again once the panel has met' after the 2026-07-25 note; narrative tension only, rejection time is not modeled. Counterexamples tried: a conforming app reading markers literally cannot fail any criterion because of the seed; a broken app cannot gain credit from seed contents (no probe values or answers embedded). Static row, fully verifiable from bytes; no runtime evidence required.
